**Interviewer:** Thank you for meeting with us for this session. I would like to begin with how performance and breaches are presented to the board.

**J. Whitfield:** Certainly. We report breaches to the board every month. The reporting needs to distinguish between the different stages of the process, because the underlying issues are not all the same.

**Interviewer:** When the board pack refers to the backlog, what is included in that figure?

**J. Whitfield:** The board pack backlog counts only fast-track booking breaches: 941 referrals since 2025-10-01.

**Interviewer:** So that figure is specifically about fast-track booking, rather than every overdue item in the programme?

**J. Whitfield:** That is correct. It is the board number we have always used. It should not be read as a complete measure of every type of breach or delay.

**Interviewer:** You mentioned that many of the breaches are related to grading. Does the same distinction apply when you look at photographs that have not received a result?

**J. Whitfield:** We look at those separately. The distribution is not even across the area, and the location of the outstanding photographs is important when we review the position.

**Interviewer:** Which districts or sites do those photographs cluster in?

**J. Whitfield:** Of the photographs that never got a result, 47% are in Hill Counties and River Districts.

**Interviewer:** Does that concentration change how you interpret the overall position?

**J. Whitfield:** It means the headline figure needs to be considered alongside its distribution. A single total can conceal where the pressure is greatest, so we need to keep the geographical pattern visible in the discussion.

**Interviewer:** That is helpful. To confirm the record, this interview is with you in your role as Screening Programme Manager, and it was held on 2026-10-07.

**J. Whitfield:** Yes, that is correct.
